secret_text: {name} stares at their hands. 'There was a patient, Day 1. Twenty-three years old. Shrapnel in the abdomen. I could have saved them. I chose to save someone else instead — someone with better odds. The twenty-three-year-old died alone in the hallway.'
forgiveness_outcome: The other survivor takes {name}'s hands. 'You made the call a doctor has to make. The person you saved — they're probably alive because of you.' {name} exhales for what feels like the first time in months.
grudge_outcome: 'You played God,' the other survivor says coldly. '{name} looks away. Some confessions aren't met with grace.'

secret_text: {name} speaks in a flat, rehearsed tone. 'My squad was ordered to clear a civilian shelter. They said there were hostiles inside. There weren't. It was just families. We realized too late.'
forgiveness_outcome: 'You were following orders in an impossible situation,' the other survivor says. 'What matters is what you do now — with the survivors who are still here.'
grudge_outcome: The other survivor steps back. 'How many?' they ask. {name} can't answer. The silence between them becomes a permanent wall.

secret_text: {name} admits quietly: 'I've been taking morphine from the supply. Not much — just enough to sleep. I know we might need it for someone who's really hurt. I just... I couldn't take the dreams anymore.'
forgiveness_outcome: 'We've all found ways to cope,' the other survivor says. 'But let's find you a better one. Together.' They sit with {name} until dawn.
grudge_outcome: 'That morphine could have saved someone in withdrawal,' the other survivor says. 'Someone who was actually trying to get clean.' {name} nods. They have no defense.

secret_text: {name}'s voice breaks: 'I had two children. The evacuation only had room for one — I had to choose. I chose the younger one. My oldest... I told them I'd come back. I didn't come back.'
forgiveness_outcome: 'No parent should ever have to make that choice,' the other survivor says, holding {name}. 'Your child knew you loved them. That's the only thing that matters.'
grudge_outcome: The other survivor is silent for a long time. 'I was the child left behind,' they finally say. 'My parents chose my brother. I survived anyway.' The shared wound doesn't heal — it just becomes visible.

secret_text: {name} confesses: 'The generator that failed on Day 17 — that wasn't an accident. I rigged it to fail so I'd be the only one who could fix it. I was afraid they'd throw me out if I wasn't useful.'
forgiveness_outcome: 'Fear makes us do stupid things,' the other survivor says. 'But you've fixed more than you've broken since then. We all know that.'
grudge_outcome: 'People could have frozen that night because of you,' the other survivor says. 'How do I trust anything you fix now?' The question hangs in the air, unanswered.

secret_text: {name} admits: 'In the first winter, when we ran out of fuel — I burned books. I burned my own books to keep the children warm. I told them they were damaged anyway. They weren't damaged. They were perfectly good books.'
forgiveness_outcome: 'You kept children alive with paper and ink,' the other survivor says. 'Any author would call that the highest use of their work.' {name} smiles weakly. They'd never thought of it that way.
grudge_outcome: 'Books are irreplaceable,' the other survivor says. 'So are children. I don't know which side of this I'm on.' The ambiguity is almost worse than condemnation.

secret_text: {name} whispers: 'My name isn't really... the one you know. I took someone else's papers when the camp was overrun. They were already dead. I just needed a new name to get into the safe zone.'
forgiveness_outcome: 'Names are just words,' the other survivor says. 'We know who you are by what you've done since you got here. That's your real name.'
grudge_outcome: 'That dead person's family might still be looking for them,' the other survivor says. 'Ever think of that?' {name} hasn't slept well since the confession.

secret_text: {name} stares at the floor: 'The blackout on Day 23 — that was me. I was running an unauthorized line to my bunk, trying to keep a small heater going. The whole grid tripped. I never told anyone it was my fault.'
forgiveness_outcome: 'You've kept the lights on every day since,' the other survivor says. 'One mistake doesn't erase a hundred fixes.'
grudge_outcome: 'People panicked in the dark that night,' the other survivor says. 'Someone got hurt. That's on you.' {name} nods slowly. They knew this was coming.
